policy: Spare home CPU always has a next job. Pop highest priority_value node, run it at full fidelity, ingest into runs/matrix.db, mark done. Never run a node at reduced fidelity without noting fidelity in the cell.

nodes.why: 72-label real-world intent menu. Julia's card only published a top-16 shortlist workaround; native 72-way fills the known weak-case cell with their actual weights. Router needs to know where big-menu intent routing breaks per arm.
nodes.est_cost: jev ~$0.40 at lockfile rates; others CPU-only

nodes.why: Their card claims multilingual scenario strength; en-US already showed 87%->50% on wording. A few locales tells us if en was the outlier or the norm. Router cares: multilingual intent is real traffic.
nodes.est_cost: CPU-heavy on ngram; run one locale at a time

nodes.why: Julia's one clean win is 6-way affect on short text. Before the router reserves a Julia lane for mood, map where that lane edges end: 27-label GoEmotions and a noisier crowdsource set bound the specialty.
Every new open decision-model release gets the full existing bench battery cold. The matrix only stays honest if arms are added on release, not ad hoc.
Jev's CLINC150 cell is partial (4100/5500, hosted stop). A finished cell closes the last hole in the original board.
